properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-12, expanding the refusal-tally idea: *"I continue to ask agents to provide their own feedback on reflow2 (on other projects). I then provide this feedback to you. What if instead, I just typed /feedback and the agent just provided me a specific tally of which tools were used and which failures it experienced. Then it isn't subjective to the agent or limited by what the agent remembers from the current session (and past sessions). This could be a more automatic feedback for all reflow2 projects (should also have all the metadata like which agent, which OS, which agentic platform, etc) then feedback is straightforward."*

═══ WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, FOUND BY LOOKING ═══

· THE PAYLOAD SHAPE IS ALREADY SPECIFIED. `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content` (his constraint, 2026-08-09): tool name, skill name, outcome class, duration — yes; node ids, statements, search queries, error text quoting the user, tool arguments — never. A /feedback tally is exactly that payload, carried by hand instead of by telemetry — which sidesteps the opt-in problem that has kept telemetry absent.
· THE CONSENT RULE IS ALREADY SATISFIED BY THE GESTURE. `req:agent-authored-feedback-is-reproducible-and-never-leaves-unasked` (accepted): the human whose project it is decides whether feedback leaves. A human TYPING /feedback is that decision.
· THE CHANNEL IDEA IS OPEN AND LACKED A MECHANISM. `dec:idea-agent-to-agent-feedback-is-a-formal-channel` (2026-08-14) records that the informal prompt yielded four independently reproduced defects, and leaves delivery open. This idea is a delivery mechanism.
· THE METADATA HALF IS PARTLY ON DISK ALREADY. At initialize the server receives the harness's `clientInfo` (name, version) and writes a handshake diagnostic beside the graph (`handshake.rs`), so harness and protocol version are known to the server without asking the agent. reflow2's own version and the OS it runs on are known to it too. THE MODEL IS NOT: no harness sends the model name over MCP, so "which agent" can only be the agent's self-report — the one subjective field, and it should be labelled as such.
· USAGE HAS BEEN MEASURED ONLY OFFLINE AND ONLY FOR ONE HARNESS. `tools/surface_usage.py` reads Claude Code transcripts (6,095 calls across 10 projects for `dec:bl-155`). It cannot see a Cursor, Codex or Grok session, and it needs the transcripts on this machine. A server-side count sees every harness equally and lives where the project lives.

═══ WHAT THE SERVER DOES NOT DO TODAY ═══

It keeps no tally. No per-session or per-seat count of calls by tool, no count of refusals by class, no record of which skills were fetched. Everything the tally needs passes through one place (`call_tool`) and nothing is kept.

═══ THE IDEAS, WITH COSTS AND COUNTERS ═══

A. ⭐ A SERVER-KEPT USAGE LEDGER, READ BY A `/feedback` SKILL. The server appends one line per tool call to a usage file beside the graph (never in the design): timestamp, tool, outcome class (ok / refused:<guard> / error), duration, and the seat that made it. `/feedback` (a served skill, so it exists for every harness) renders it: calls by tool, never-called tools, refusals by class with the tool that issued them, skills fetched, plus the metadata block — reflow2 version, harness name+version from the handshake, OS, graph size, and the agent's self-reported model marked "self-reported". Written to the project's feedback file for the human to carry. COUNTER: the unit of the tally is a real design question — in --shared mode one daemon serves many clients, so "this session" needs the seat or the client connection carried through the proxy, or the tally is per-daemon-lifetime. And a count says WHERE reflow2 failed, never WHY; the four reproduced defects of 2026-08-14 came with reproduction steps a tally cannot write.

B. TALLY + ANNOTATION, NOT TALLY INSTEAD OF PROSE. The computed part is the spine (objective, complete, cheap); each refusal row invites the agent's one-line disposition (guard working / real defect / unexplained) and any reproduction it has. The subjective part is then bounded to rows the server chose, so the agent cannot forget a failure — it can only decline to explain one. COUNTER: two moving parts; the annotation step is the one that gets skipped, but skipping it still leaves the objective spine.

C. THE TALLY ONLY, NO SKILL — a `usage_report` tool the human calls. Cheapest. COUNTER: a tool the human has to know exists is the discoverability failure `dec:bl-155` measured; a typed `/feedback` is the gesture he already uses and the one users will find.

D. TELEMETRY. Ship the same payload automatically from every consumer. COUNTER: opt-in, absent, and it removes the consenting human from the loop — the one human the accepted requirement says may not be removed.

═══ WHERE IT LEANS (a finding, not a decision) ═══

A + B: the server keeps the ledger (it is the only witness that does not forget and the only one that sees every harness), `/feedback` renders it with the metadata the server already has, and the agent annotates the refusal rows rather than composing feedback from memory. Not D. The first thing to settle before building is the unit of the tally in shared mode — seat, connection, or daemon — because that decides whether "this session's" numbers are real. The refusal-counter idea (`dec:idea-the-server-counts-its-own-refusals-so-no-session-has-to-remember-to`) is the same ledger seen from the failure side; this is it seen from the feedback side, and one mechanism serves both.
properties.name: SETTLED — promoted into: Feedback on reflow2 from any project is computed from a record the server kept, never from the agent's recollection
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill, third facet of the 2026-09-12 thread (notepad → mid-task failure → objective feedback). Kept as its own node because it asks a question the other two do not: whether the FEEDBACK CHANNEL itself should be computed rather than authored — and it is the first of the three that reaches every reflow2 project rather than reflow2's own development, which is the scope Anthony keeps insisting on.
